issues.title: [Enhancement] Add Command-Line Arguments to Benchmark Scripts
issues.body:
## Description

Currently, `benchmark.py` and `multi_agent_benchmark.py` have hardcoded simulation lengths (e.g., `NUM_WEEKS = 52`). To make them more flexible for testing, we should allow these values to be set via command-line arguments.

## Steps
- [ ] Add Python's built-in `argparse` library to `tests/benchmark.py`.
- [ ] Define a command-line argument, e.g., `--weeks`, that allows a user to specify the number of weeks for the simulation.
- [ ] Replace the hardcoded `NUM_WEEKS_TO_SIMULATE` constant with the value from the command-line argument.
- [ ] Repeat the same process for `tests/multi_agent_benchmark.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A user can run `python3 -m tests.benchmark --weeks 20` to run a 20-week simulation.
- [ ] If no argument is provided, the script should default to 52 weeks.
- [ ] The script provides a `--help` message explaining the available arguments.

## References
- `tests/benchmark.py`
- `tests/multi_agent_benchmark.py`
- [Python `argparse` tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/howto/argparse.html)

issues.title: Make `transpile` accept a `Target` as the `backend` argument
issues.body:
### What should we add?

The `transpile` function's signature looks a bit like like
```python
def transpile(qc: QuantumCircuit, backend: Backend, target: Target, *_) -> QuantumCircuit
```
and it's commonly called as `transpile(qc, backend)`.  However, it would be nice too if we could recognise when a `Target` is passed positionally as the second argument as well, and then simply behave as if the user had specified `backend=None, target=target`; when building custom compilation targets, it's very rare to want to build a `Backend` wrapper to surround it.

We should raise a `TypeError` if the second positional argument is a `Target` and the `target` keyword is passed by other means as well. 

`generate_preset_pass_manager` already supports this mode of operation, so this would be making it consistent.

issues.title: 🚀 [UPLOAD PAGE] INSTRUCTIONAL SNACKBAR
issues.body: This issue focuses on implementing the Instructional Snackbar in the Upload Page ***(when user opens the Upload Page)*** that appears briefly when a user opens the app ***for the first time after installing it***. The snackbar is designed to introduce new users to a key interaction pattern — "Tap & Hold to Edit Wallpaper" — making the experience more intuitive from the start. - First-Time Trigger Only: The snackbar should display only once per fresh install of the app. If the user reinstalls the app, it should appear again. - Delayed Appearance: Once the user opens the app, the snackbar should wait 0.5 seconds before appearing — giving a subtle, non-intrusive feel. - Auto-Dismiss Duration: The snackbar remains visible for 3 seconds before automatically disappearing. - Minimal and Friendly Design: The snackbar displays a clean, centered message — “Tap & Hold to Edit Wallpaper” — that blends well with the overall UI without disrupting the user’s experience. - No Manual Dismissal: The snackbar vanishes automatically — no close button or tap-to-dismiss behavior required. - Visual Consistency: The design should follow the current WallGodds visual language: soft edges, centered alignment, and a friendly tone. If you face any issues while working on this page or have questions, feel free to reach out to us on [Discord](https://discord.gg/kTQ5KWANp8) — we’re always happy to help!

issues.title: Dashboard filters allow creating bi-directional dependencies in an unexpected way with value filters
issues.body:
### Bug description

When configuring dashboard filters with the "Values are dependent on other filters" option, the system prevents creating bi-directional dependencies upfront by showing a "Cyclic dependency detected" message. However, it allows creating the same dependency indirectly after saving the initial filter configuration.

1. If Filter A is set to depend on Filter B, the system blocks setting Filter B to depend on Filter A immediately, showing a "Cyclic dependency detected" message.
2. However, if Filter A is saved with the dependency on Filter B, the system later allows editing Filter B to create the reverse dependency, effectively forming a bi-directional (cyclic) dependency.

This behavior is inconsistent and might lead to unexpected filter behavior. It appears to contradict the intended prevention of cyclic dependencies.
How to reproduce the bug

1. Create a dashboard filter (e.g., Filter A) with a dependency on another filter (e.g., Filter B) by enabling the Values are dependent on other filters option.
2. Save the filter configuration.
3. Open the dashboard filter configuration again, select Filter B, and set it to depend on Filter A.

The system should prevent bi-directional (cyclic) dependencies for all filter types, not just date filters. Users should not be able to create a cyclic dependency by editing the filters after saving the initial configuration.

## Actual results

The platform allows creating cyclic dependencies indirectly after the initial configuration, even though it prevents it upfront. This behavior is inconsistent and may lead to unexpected filter behavior.

### What you would like to be added?

We should add AGENTS.md file to Kubeflow SDK, this is a unified Markdown file that coding agents can use to understand a codebase.
It's has already been adopted by over 28k open source [projects](https://github.com/search?q=path%3AAGENTS.md&type=code)

### Why is this needed?

This will improve the development experience for developers using AI tools, as they'll have better context about our specific project structure and conventions.
It's also becoming a standard practice in the open source community, [PyTorch](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [LangGraph](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langgraph/blob/main/AGENTS.md), [LangChain](https://github.com/langchain-ai/langchain/blob/master/CLAUDE.md), and others already provide Markdown files for coding agents.
The file should include information about our project structure, key dependencies, coding conventions and any Kubeflow SDK specific context that would help AI understand how to work with our code

Currently, w.r.t. PostgreSQL policies, a user can:

issues.title: Deprecation warning in MLflow docs: fillna(method=...) in pandas 3.0+
issues.body:
### Willingness to contribute

Yes. I can contribute a documentation fix independently.

### URL(s) with the issue

https://github.com/mlflow/mlflow/blob/master/docs/docs/classic-ml/getting-started/logging-first-model/step5-synthetic-data.mdx

### Description of proposal (what needs changing)

The documentation currently uses:

df["previous_days_demand"].fillna(method="bfill", inplace=True)

This raises warnings in pandas 3.0+:

- Using `fillna(method=...)` is deprecated.  
- Using `inplace=True` on a Series slice causes a chained assignment warning.  

**Proposed fix:**  
Replace with:

df["previous_days_demand"] = df["previous_days_demand"].bfill()

This avoids deprecation warnings and is the recommended modern pandas usage.

issues.title: Deterministic seed for sampling
issues.body:
A key requirement for reproducibility is to have a deterministic random seed. For example, if I run the following code

```python
@squin.kernel
def coinflip():
    qubit = squin.qubit.new(1)[0]
    squin.gate.h(qubit)
    return squin.qubit.measure(qubit)
emulator = StackMemorySimulator()
task = emulator.task(coinflip)
bit = task.run()
```

The variable `bit` will be random. But if we want a reproducible script e.g. to send to others, we should ensure that everything is run deterministically, e.g. reproducibly.

So, my ask would be to set a seed for pyqrack (and any classical randomness?) somewhere in this workflow, either
```python
StackMemorySimulator(SEED=0)   # a
emulator.task(coinflip, SEED=0)# b
task.run(SEED=0) # c
```

```sway
contract;

abi Demo {
    fn get_count() -> u64;
}

impl Demo for Contract {
    fn get_count() -> u64 {
        5
    }
}
```

Working command (without wallet - uses default signer - which has funds..):
```bash
forc call --abi ./out/release/demo-abi.json $CONTRACT_ADDRESS get_count
```

Failing command (with wallet):
```bash
forc call --abi ./out/release/demo-abi.json $CONTRACT_ADDRESS get_count --wallet
```

thread 'main' panicked at /Users/runner/work/sway/sway/forc-plugins/forc-client/src/op/call/missing_contracts.rs:32:10:

issues.title: Bug: broker.subscriber do not execute due to WeakSet
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**

A subscriber that is created and not persisted outside of the `broker.subscribers`
will not execute due to the broker only storing the subscriber within a WeakSet.

**How to reproduce**

One would expect message1 to raise, however only message2 does.

```python
from faststream import FastStream

async def test_should_raise_message1(
    app: StreamApp,
    broker: KafkaBroker,
) -> None:
    async def handle(msg: str) -> None:
        raise Exception(msg)

    broker.subscriber("topic1")(handle)
    this_is_persisted = broker.subscriber("topic2")(handle)

    async with KafkaTestBroker(broker):
        await broker.publish("message1", "topic1")
        await broker.publish("message2", "topic2")
```

**Expected behavior**

This behaviour is different than versions < 0.6.0 and a bit of a footgun ... There 
may be a reason for this that is not obvious to me, and if so, then perhaps 
a big **warning** might be helpful in the documentation.

**Observed behavior**

A subscriber ( and a provider for that matter ) that is not otherwise persisted
is lost and not invoked even if registered with the broker.

**Additional context**

In my use-case, the subscribers are all registered within a `create_app`
function and the references are therefore never persisted.

This was previously needed so that apps could be more easily testable 
and configurable and is more so now that subscribers seem to have mutable
state ( i.e. the .configs array ).

issues.title: [ENH] `torch` / `lightning` integration
issues.body:
It would be nice to have integration with basic `torch` and `lightning` tuning workflows, to allow autoML style tuning.

This would require a `BaseExperiment` descendant class `TorchExperiment` which takes a `DataLoader`, a `LightningModule`, and a `Trainer`, performs a training run, and returns the validation loss/score. Also see the extension template https://github.com/SimonBlanke/Hyperactive/blob/main/extension_templates/experiments.py

Since tuning is not API preserving in `torch` / `lightning`, I would suggest an additional function that produces parameters for a tuned network, or the initialized tuned network with said parameters - e.g., `tune_lightning(optimizer: BaseOptimizer, loader, module, trainer)`? Or is it clear enough to construct the optimizer and call `solve`?

Comments appreciated on the design.

Set the log level (`info` | `warn` | `error` | `silent`).

The same as [Rsbuild](https://rsbuild.rs/guide/basic/cli#common-flags):

```
rspeedy --log-level silent

rspeedy --log-level error

And a new `logLevel` configuration:

```js
import { defineConfig } from '@lynx-js/rspeedy'

export default defineConfig({
  logLevel: 'error',
})
```

## Tasks

- [ ] Create a new ```generalFormPDEScript``` solver for 1D differential equations, where the differential equation will be converted into the "weak", integral, form.

issues.title: Job output files are not cleaned up after job completion or cancellation
issues.body:
## Problem Description

The CipherSwarmAgent does not properly clean up output files when hashcat jobs are finished or cancelled. This leads to:

- Disk space accumulation over time
- Potential security issues with sensitive hash data remaining on disk  
- Storage bloat in production environments
- Orphaned .pot files and other hashcat outputs

## Current State Analysis

Based on the codebase review:
- The agent has basic PID file cleanup via `cleanupLockFile()` in `lib/agent/agent.go`
- However, there's no corresponding cleanup for job output files
- Hashcat sessions may create various output files (.pot, .out, etc.) that persist after completion

## Current Behavior
- Job output files remain on the filesystem after job completion
- No cleanup mechanism is triggered when jobs are cancelled or fail
- Files accumulate indefinitely without manual intervention
- Only PID files are currently cleaned up on agent shutdown

## Expected Behavior
- Output files should be automatically deleted when a hashcat job completes successfully
- Files should be cleaned up when a job is cancelled or fails
- Temporary files should have a maximum retention period as a safeguard
- Cleanup should be handled gracefully with proper error handling

## Impact
- **Severity**: Medium - affects system resources and security
- **Environment**: All environments where agents process hashcat jobs
- **Users Affected**: System administrators and users running long-term cracking operations

## Proposed Solution

### Implementation Areas
1. **Hashcat Session Cleanup**: Extend session management to track and cleanup output files
2. **Job Lifecycle Hooks**: Add cleanup logic to job completion/cancellation handlers  
3. **File Tracking**: Implement a mechanism to track all created output files
4. **Graceful Cleanup**: Use Go's `defer` statements for guaranteed cleanup
5. **Configuration**: Add settings for cleanup behavior and retention policies

### Technical Approach
- Extend the existing `cleanupLockFile` pattern to handle job output files
- Add cleanup methods to hashcat session management
- Implement file tracking in job processing logic
- Add proper error handling to prevent cleanup failures
- Consider using Go's `os.RemoveAll` for directory cleanup

## Files to Investigate
- `lib/agent/agent.go` - Main agent logic with existing cleanup patterns
- Hashcat session management code
- Job processing and lifecycle management

## Additional Context
This issue is critical for production deployments where agents may process many jobs over extended periods.

issues.title: 🧪 Implement Comprehensive Unit Testing Framework for Core Agent Functions
issues.body:
# Add Unit Tests for Core Functions

To ensure the reliability and stability of our CipherSwarmAgent codebase, it is crucial to add comprehensive unit tests for all core functions. This will help catch bugs early, improve code quality, and facilitate future development and maintenance.

## Current State Analysis

The CipherSwarmAgent project currently lacks comprehensive unit test coverage for its core functionality. Based on codebase analysis, the following critical functions require unit testing:

### Core Functions Requiring Tests

#### Agent Lifecycle Functions
- `Start()` - Main agent startup and initialization
- `AuthenticateAgent()` - Agent authentication with the server
- `handleNonExhaustedError()` - Error handling for non-exhausted attack scenarios
- `runTestTask()` - Test task execution logic

#### Display Functions
- `DisplayStartup()` - Startup message display
- `DisplayAuthenticated()` - Authentication success display  
- `DisplayNewTask()` - New task notification display
- `DisplayNewAttack()` - New attack notification display
- `DisplayInactive()` - Inactive state display
- `DisplayShuttingDown()` - Shutdown process display

#### Utility Functions
- `findHashcatBinary()` - Hashcat binary location detection
- Configuration and settings management functions
- HTTP client and API communication functions

## Proposed Solution

### 1. Testing Framework Setup
- Use Go's built-in `testing` package as the primary testing framework
- Implement table-driven tests where appropriate for comprehensive coverage
- Use `testify` library for enhanced assertions and mocking capabilities

### 2. Test Structure Organization
```
tests/
├── unit/
│   ├── agent_test.go           # Core agent functionality
│   ├── display_test.go         # Display functions
│   ├── auth_test.go            # Authentication logic
│   ├── hashcat_test.go         # Hashcat binary management
│   └── utils_test.go           # Utility functions
├── integration/
│   └── agent_integration_test.go
├── mocks/
│   ├── http_client_mock.go
│   ├── file_system_mock.go
│   └── server_mock.go
└── testdata/
    ├── config_samples/
    └── response_samples/
```

### 3. Testing Strategy

#### Unit Test Coverage
- **Target**: Minimum 80% code coverage for core functions
- **Approach**: Test individual functions in isolation using dependency injection and mocking
- **Focus Areas**:
  - Happy path scenarios
  - Error conditions and edge cases
  - Boundary value testing
  - Input validation

#### Mock Strategy
- Mock external dependencies (HTTP clients, file system operations, system calls)
- Create test doubles for server interactions
- Use dependency injection to make functions testable

#### Test Data Management
- Store test configuration files and sample responses in `testdata/` directory
- Use golden files for output comparison where appropriate
- Implement test helpers for common setup and teardown operations

### 4. Implementation Plan

#### Phase 1: Foundation (Week 1)
- [ ] Set up testing infrastructure and dependencies
- [ ] Create mock interfaces for external dependencies
- [ ] Implement basic test utilities and helpers

#### Phase 2: Core Function Tests (Week 2-3)
- [ ] `AuthenticateAgent()` - Test authentication flow with various server responses
- [ ] `findHashcatBinary()` - Test binary detection across different environments
- [ ] `Start()` - Test agent initialization with different configurations

#### Phase 3: Display and Utility Functions (Week 4)
- [ ] All `Display*()` functions - Test output formatting and console interactions
- [ ] `handleNonExhaustedError()` and `runTestTask()` - Test error handling and task execution

#### Phase 4: Integration and CI/CD (Week 5)
- [ ] Integration tests for complete workflows
- [ ] CI/CD pipeline integration
- [ ] Performance and benchmarking tests

### 5. CI/CD Integration

#### GitHub Actions Workflow
```yaml
name: Test Coverage
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v4
        with:
          go-version: '1.21'
      
      - name: Run Tests
        run: |
          go test -v -race -coverprofile=coverage.out ./...
          go tool cover -html=coverage.out -o coverage.html
      
      - name: Check Coverage
        run: |
          COVERAGE=$(go tool cover -func=coverage.out | grep total | awk '{print $3}' | sed 's/%//')
          if (( $(echo "$COVERAGE < 80" | bc -l) )); then
            echo "Coverage $COVERAGE% is below 80%"
            exit 1
          fi
      
      - name: Upload Coverage Reports
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v3
        with:
          file: ./coverage.out
```

### 6. Success Metrics

- [ ] **Code Coverage**: Achieve minimum 80% test coverage for core functions
- [ ] **CI Integration**: All tests pass automatically on commits and PRs  
- [ ] **Performance**: Test suite completes in under 2 minutes
- [ ] **Maintainability**: Tests are well-documented and easy to understand
- [ ] **Reliability**: Tests consistently pass across different environments

### 7. Additional Considerations

#### Testing Best Practices
- Follow Go testing conventions and idioms
- Use meaningful test names that describe the scenario
- Keep tests independent and avoid test interdependencies
- Use setup/teardown functions for common test initialization

#### Documentation
- Document testing patterns and conventions in `TESTING.md`
- Provide examples of how to write tests for new functions
- Include troubleshooting guide for common testing issues

### 8. Dependencies

Add testing dependencies to `go.mod`:
```go
// Testing dependencies
github.com/stretchr/testify v1.8.4
github.com/golang/mock v1.6.0
github.com/jarcoal/httpmock v1.3.1
```

## Resources

- [Go Testing Documentation](https://golang.org/pkg/testing/)
- [Testify Framework](https://github.com/stretchr/testify)
- [Go Testing Best Practices](https://go.dev/doc/tutorial/add-a-test)
- [Table-Driven Tests in Go](https://go.dev/wiki/TableDrivenTests)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All listed core functions have comprehensive unit tests
- [ ] Minimum 80% code coverage achieved
- [ ] All tests pass in CI/CD pipeline
- [ ] Tests include both happy path and error scenarios
- [ ] Mock external dependencies appropriately
- [ ] Test documentation is complete and clear

issues.title: Add idempotency support for state‑changing endpoints (fund transfer, deposit, withdrawal)
issues.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
When a client makes a state‑changing API request (e.g. transferring funds, making a withdrawal or deposit), network errors or timeouts may cause the client to retry the request. Currently, the API does not enforce idempotency, so retrying the same request can lead to duplicate transactions or unintended multiple side‑effects. This can cause financial discrepancies and poor user experience.

---

**Describe the solution you'd like**
- Introduce an `Idempotency‑Key` (or similarly named) header for endpoints that modify state.  
- Maintain a persistent store (e.g. an `idempotency_records` table) with entries like: key, user identifier, endpoint, request payload or hash, timestamp, status, and the response returned.  
- On receiving a request with a key that matches a previous one (same user + same endpoint + same payload—or acceptable equivalent), return the stored response instead of re‑processing the operation.  
- Ensure the write of the idempotency record and the financial operation are done atomically to avoid race conditions (e.g. two identical requests arriving almost simultaneously).  
- Define a retention / expiration policy (TTL) for idempotency records so that storage doesn’t grow unbounded.  
- Update API documentation and the Postman collection to describe how clients should use the idempotency key.

---

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
- Relying fully on client‑side uniqueness (e.g. clients generate unique IDs and avoid retries) — this is risky because clients might reuse keys by mistake or fail to generate correctly.  
- Performing de‑duplication based on heuristics like matching timestamp + amount + recipient etc. — fragile, especially when payloads differ slightly.  
- Only implementing idempotency for a subset of endpoints (for example, only transfers) — while this reduces scope, it leaves other operations vulnerable to duplicate side‑effects.

---

**Additional context**
- This feature is important in financial systems to prevent accidental duplicate operations and to comply with expectations of reliability.  
- Tests should be added (unit + integration) to simulate retries and verify no duplicate execution.  
- Consider concurrency pitfalls: e.g. two identical requests arriving almost at the same time with the same idempotency key.  
- Might also need to consider what to do if the same key is used but with different payloads — error vs treat it as new vs some sort of mismatch detection.

issues.title: login button no working
Register xmpp protocol handler
issues.body:
## Steps to reproduce

- On any other website, or application, click on an `xmpp:` uri. e.g., `xmpp:discuss@conference.conversejs.org?join` (github won't convert this into a link)

## What I expect

A  popup like the following appears, and conversejs is available in the list:
![launch-application](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/138302/46888066-edf7a180-ce4e-11e8-9fb1-e57ea75dfc80.png)

Movim also displays the url of the instance, that I have greyed out here. But I assume it's just the browser adding some context to the entry, saying which website has registered the handler.

## What happens

Converse doesn't appear in the list.

## Misc

Implementation wise, the API to use seems to be [navigator.registerProtocolHandler](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Navigator/registerProtocolHandler/Web-based_protocol_handlers)

This is what it looks like in Firefox:
![add-application](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/138302/46888698-be499900-ce50-11e8-9916-b3e4d92d686d.png)


A few things to consider before implementing:
- Not all conversejs instance will want to use this. I hardly see a need for a customer support platform for example, they will certainly want it off. The feature should probably be behind a configuration flag?
- Every conversejs instance I navigate to will start asking me to register the protocol handler. Is that something we want?
- Remembering that the user didn't add the handler might also be useful to avoid spamming them, (that happens too often in web applications).
- In the future, if this is implemented, removing the `registerProtocolHandler` call doesn't mean the handler is gone. I don't think there is a way to remove it even, from the application itself. That seems to be a user action, in the browser settings.

## Description
Hooks are stateful objects, which enables users to, for example, store the context in the `after_context_created` hook and use it later in a hook that doesn't receive it:

```python
class SomeHook:
    @hook_spec
    def after_context_created(self, context):
       ...
       self.my_azure_config = xxx

    @hook_spec
    def before_pipeline_run(self, pipeline):
       do_something_about_my_pipeline(pipeline, self.my_azure_config)
```

(code sample by @antonymilne )

We should better document this.

Follow up from gh-506 and other discussions, see for example https://www.linen.dev/s/kedro/t/12112601/does-anyone-know-if-there-is-a-reason-why-we-could-not-pass-#4e36a67f-36d3-4354-a3d5-4347a59ef28f

issues.title: All staging hosts should be first wave
issues.body:
# Context

At present we divide all our servers into three “waves” that we use to control when major upgrades, e.g. 24.11 --> 25.05 are executed. We also have a staging & main branch of our Nix code.

The default wave for all new machines is the middle wave, while the first wave is dev machines and ‘penguins’ that highlight config issues early in the release cycle.

We have different JSON files for managing which machine goes where, but we should unify them. 

All staging machines are first wave, not all first wave machines are on staging!

# Code

See: [host-config.nix](https://github.com/MSF-OCB/org-nixos-config-public/blob/main/host-config.nix), [waves-and-staging-hosts.json](https://github.com/MSF-OCB/org-nixos-config-public/blob/main/org-config/json/waves-and-staging-hosts.json).

# Deliverables

A PR with a refactored host-config.nix to and waves-and-staging-hosts.json to be more DRY (Don’t Repeat Yourself): hostnames should only be present once in the file.

**Stretch goal:** all the info in waves-and-staging-hosts.json should probably be in the “hosts/*.nix” file, so each host file defines the branch and wave.
We will support by providing test hardware.

# Impact
The next time we install a new dev machine, we won’t forget to add it in two different places in the same file.

issues.title: [Clang] Add __builtin_bswapg
issues.body: Currently Clang has `__builtin_bswap{16,32,64}`. It would be great if there was a `__builtin_bswapg` that works on any integral types that has a multiple of 16 bits as well as a single byte, which would simply be the identity. This would avoid a long `if constexpr` chain when implementing `std::byteswap`, which uses the same codegen path in the end anyways. It would also make it trivial to add support for `_BitInt` as well.

issues.title: [bug] Status component uses incorrect query param for session lookup
issues.body:
**Describe the bug**
The Status component in the client currently checks for an active session by filtering with the `macaddr` query parameter. However, the OpenWISP RADIUS API endpoint does not support filtering by `macaddr`; it expects `calling_station_id` as the query param for MAC address-based filtering.

**Relevant code:**
- [`client/components/status/status.js` (uses `macaddr` as query param)](https://github.com/openwisp/openwisp-wifi-login-pages/blob/e1ef7e0f7ad910faf51ff04c8ec878a865835e90/client/components/status/status.js#L217-L231)
- [The RADIUS API (`openwisp_radius/api/views.py`) expects `calling_station_id` for MAC address filtering.](https://github.com/openwisp/openwisp-radius/blob/4d9d85195624b60f157339e8884ac45539918f30/openwisp_radius/api/views.py#L808-L848)

**Steps To Reproduce**
1. Attempt to retrieve radius sessions for a user with a specific MAC address.
2. Observe that the frontend sends a `macaddr` query param to the API.
3. The API does not filter sessions as expected because it does not recognize `macaddr`.

**Expected behavior**
The frontend should use the `calling_station_id` query parameter when requesting sessions by MAC address, matching the OpenWISP RADIUS API's expectations.

issues.body:
### Description

The documentation for the aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm resource is fantastic, as one would expect from any of the hashicorp documentation, but the examples are fairly basic.

It's possible to write a SQL-style statement to collect and filter metrics, based on available dimensions.  I struggled with how to do this for a while simply because I didn't know what to ask.  For instance, it's possible to add a metric_query block to a resource, like this:

```hcl
  metric_query {
    id          = "m1"
    expression  = "SELECT MAX(DBLoadRelativeToNumVCPUs) FROM SCHEMA(\"AWS/RDS\", DBInstanceIdentifier) WHERE DBInstanceIdentifier != '${aws_rds_cluster_instance.data_warehouse[0].id}' GROUP BY DBInstanceIdentifier ORDER BY MAX() ASC"
    period      = 60
    return_data = true
    label       = "Max DB Load Relative to vCPUs"
  }
```

The result is that I can filter a specific RDS instance that I *don't* want alarms on (or perhaps I want less sensitive alarms, just for that instance).

I learned this by playing around in the AWS console, but I didn't know how to take that newly gained knowledge and actually apply it with Terraform.  

I used AWS Bedrock (Cline) and got hilariously made-up results, then I passed what I knew to Google Gemini and it nailed it.  Still, it would be great if there were an example of something complex, like this, so users would know they can specify pretty much any query as a query expression.

issues.title: ✏️ Update Student View Page – Add Edit (Pencil) Icon for Admin Access Only
issues.body:
# ✏️ Admin Inline Edit Feature for Student View Page

This feature allows **admin users** to update student information directly from the **Student View Page** using an inline edit interface. No modals or new pages are needed — editing happens in-place for a fast and smooth admin experience.

---

## 🔗 Frontend Location

- **Page URL:** [`https://www.growrichmindset.in/admin/Students`](https://www.growrichmindset.in/admin/Students)
- **Access:** 🔐 Protected route – only accessible to authenticated admin users.

---

## 🎯 Feature Overview

### 🎨 UI Changes

- A **pencil icon (✏️)** is displayed to each student’s record in the Form Title.
- When an admin clicks this icon:
  - That specific row (or card) **enters "edit mode"**.
  - Text fields (like name, email, phone, etc.) become editable.
  - A **"Save"** button and a **"Cancel"** button are shown.
- After editing, the admin can:
  - Click **Save** to submit the changes.
  - Click **Cancel** to discard any changes and exit edit mode.

---

## 🧪 Example Use Case

1. Admin logs into the dashboard and visits the Student View Page.
2. A pencil icon is visible next to each student.
3. Admin clicks the pencil icon next to a student named "John Doe".
4. The row switches to **edit mode**, and admin updates the email and phone number.
5. Admin clicks **Save**.
6. The updated data is sent to the backend via an API call.
7. Upon success:
   - A success message is shown (e.g., "Student updated successfully").
   - The row switches back to view mode with the new data visible.

---

## 🔁 Backend API Integration

### ➤ Endpoint

- **URL:** `/api/v1/student/update`
- **Method:** `POST`
- **Access:** Protected – only for authenticated admin users

### ➤ Expected Payload

```json
{
  "studentId": "12345",
  "name": "Updated Name",
  "email": "updated.email@example.com",
  "phone": "9876543210"
}
```

### ➤ Success Response


```js
{
  "success": true,
  "message": "Student updated successfully"
}


```

## ✅ Feature Requirements

This section outlines all the required functionality and behavior for the inline student editing feature. These items must be completed for the feature to be considered done.

### 🔓 Access Control

- [x] The **Student View Page** must be accessible **only to logged-in admin users**.
- [x] The **pencil icon (✏️)** must be visible only for authenticated admins.

---

### 🖱️ UI Behavior

- [x] Each student record must show a **pencil icon** in an actions column or next to the data.
- [ ] When the admin clicks the pencil icon:
  - The selected row or section enters **inline edit mode**.
  - Editable fields (e.g., Name, Email, Phone) turn into input fields.
  - Show **Save** and **Cancel** buttons for that row.
- [ ] The **Cancel** button should:
  - Discard any unsaved changes.
  - Return the row to **view-only mode**.

---

### 💾 Data Handling

- [ ] When the **Save** button is clicked:
  - The updated data must be sent to the backend API: `POST /api/v1/student/update`.
  - Include the necessary student ID and all updated fields in the request payload.

---

### ✅ API Response Handling

- [ ] On a successful update:
  - Show a confirmation message (e.g., "Student updated successfully").
  - Exit edit mode and display the updated data in view mode.
- [ ] On an error:
  - Show a clear error message (e.g., "Failed to update student").
  - Do not exit edit mode unless **Cancel** is clicked.

issues.title: Handle negative values outisde of the lexer
issues.body:
Right now our lexer distinguish positive and negative integer literals with rule https://github.com/Lamagraph/interaction-nets-in-fpga/blob/badb312c7181a54971b2129f7822416eb282bc98/lamagraph-compiler/src/Lamagraph/Compiler/Parser/Lexer.x#L74

This breaks valid code such as
```ocaml
let f x = x-1
```
but not
```ocaml
let f x = x - 1
```
because in the first snippet `-1` is handled in lexer, while in the second one parser gives correct AST. 

Note: `TokInt` is defined as `TokInt Int`, but after fix we'll be unable to parse `-2147483648`.

issues.title: Compilation Takes a Long Time When Using Data Mapper in the Project
issues.body:
### Current Limitation

The DataMapper Mediator is very effective and often clearer than the PayloadFactory in some use cases. However, it significantly increases the compilation time in VS Code Extensions. When I click "Build and Run," Maven starts by removing all files in the "./target" directory, downloading Node.js and npm, and running "npm install" before packaging the ".car" archive. This process can take more than 10 minutes. After the initial compilation, subsequent compilations also take a long time because Node.js, npm, and the node_modules directory, which are downloaded during "npm install," are all removed as they reside in the "./target" folder. If I use DataMapper, every time I compile the project, I have to wait more than 10 minutes for downloading Node.js, npm, and running "npm install." This is quite frustrating.

### Suggested Improvement

1. Change the location of Node.js and node_modules.
2. Allow users to configure the location of Node.js and node_modules.
3. Stop removing Node.js and node_modules from the ./target folder.

### Version

4.3.0

issues.title: attach() for SocketFilter needs an enum

SocketFilter programs can be attached to a socket with two socket options:
- SO_ATTACH_BPF
- SO_ATTACH_REUSEPORT_EBPF

See: man socket(7)

We should add an enum to `attach()` for SocketFilter programs so the caller can pick the attach type they want.

The latter program type MUST return an integer - we should ensure that the SocketFilter program in aya-bpf returns one (i32 or u32 probably) and verify the behaviour of the return code in both modes of attachment so we can document any verifier hiccups. issues.title: [X86] X86FixupInstTunings - attempt to convert VPERMQri to VINSERTI128rri
issues.body:
AVX2 target shuffle combining/lowering often performs a 128-bit subvector splat as VPERMQ as this allows memory folding if the subvector had been spilled.

But for most targets if we don't use the VPERMQmi and instead lower to `VPERMQri %dst, %src, $0x44` we would have been much better off using `VINSERTI128rri %dst, %src, xmm_sub(%src), 0x1`.

X86FixupInstTunings should check the scheduler model agrees VINSERTI128rri is faster and adjusts the instruction encoding (not just the opcode but the registers and immediate need checking/adjusting as well).

issues.title: Enhance File Upload Feature Using Multer
issues.body:
# Enhance File Upload Feature Using Multer

## Description
Currently, the file upload flow requires users to manually enter a file URL. This is not user-friendly and limits usability.  
We can improve this by integrating **Multer**, a popular middleware for handling `multipart/form-data` in Node.js. With Multer, users will be able to directly upload files from their device instead of pasting URLs.  

## Proposed Solution
- Install and configure **Multer** in the backend.  
- Create an API endpoint that accepts file uploads.  
- Store uploaded files on the server (or a storage service like AWS S3/Cloudinary if needed).  
- Update the frontend to allow users to pick files from their device instead of pasting URLs.  
- Return the uploaded file path/URL from the backend and save it in the database as before.  

## Benefits
- More intuitive and user-friendly experience.  
- Reduces errors from invalid URLs.  
- Makes the platform more professional and reliable.  

## Tech Stack
- **Backend:** Node.js, Express.js, Multer  
- **Frontend:** React (for UI file selection)  

## Additional Notes
- Consider adding file type and size validation (e.g., allow only images under 5 MB).  
- For future scalability, we could integrate cloud storage.

issues.title: Support stamping in OCI labels, annotations and env
issues.body:
In rules_oci, metadata to the image can be stamped. This is extremely useful.

I would expect something like this to work:

```
image_manifest(
        ...,
        labels = {
            "org.opencontainers.image.revision": "{STABLE_BUILD_SCM_HASH_FULL}",  # TODO: Stamp it!
            "org.opencontainers.image.source": "{REPO_URL}",  # Stamp it!
            "source.path": native.package_name(),
        },
        env = {
            "GIT_SHA": "{STABLE_BUILD_SCM_HASH_FULL}",  # TODO: Stamp it!
        },
)
```

As a workaround we can use `config_fragment`, and pass a stamped json file into the image_manifest rule. Adding this to our internal macro works well, but it doesn't allow end users to append stamped labels to images.

The implementation in rules_oci relies on accepting a file (k=v per line) as input for env, labels, and annotations. That allows us to stamp the file before passing it to rules_oci.

issues.title: [BUG]: Profile colors and positions change when selecting a profile in the Profile screen
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

When selecting a profile from the "Select your profile" screen, the profile list slightly shifts and some profile colors change unexpectedly.

### Steps To Reproduce

- Open the Oppia app.
- Go to the "Select your profile" screen.
- Set up multiple profiles (more than 5).
- Scroll down and click on any profile near the bottom of the list.
- Observe that the profiles slightly shift from their original position and profile colors change.

### Expected Behavior

Profile positions and colors should remain consistent when selecting a profile.

### Screenshots/Videos

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b91a4b7-1a96-4f34-ac61-7fe639506d2e

### What device/emulator are you using?

Oppo reno 2f

### Which Android version is your device/emulator running?

Android 11

### Which version of the Oppia Android app are you using?

_No response_

### Additional Context

**Cause:**
When a profile is clicked, `onProfileClick() `updates the learner ID if it is absent. This causes the `LiveData` holding the profile list to emit a new list. Since the current adapter uses `notifyDataSetChanged()`, the entire RecyclerView reloads all items. As a result, the list briefly shows flickering, incorrect colors, and temporary item shifts.

**Proposed Solution:**
Introduce `DiffUtil`in `RecyclerViewBindingAdapter` for the `profile_recycler_view`. Since each profile has a unique id, we can use it to efficiently calculate differences and update only the changed items. This will eliminate flickering and keep profile colors stable during list updates.

**Files to Check:**
- [ProfileChooserFragmentPresenter](https://github.com/oppia/oppia-android/blob/fcb87dc79074450f90a658c9dddb186a12ab75f3/app/src/main/java/org/oppia/android/app/profile/ProfileChooserFragmentPresenter.kt#L70C7-L70C38) -> funs `onProfileClick()`, `updateLearnerIdIfAbsent()`, `computeLoginRoute()`
- [ProfilemanagementController](https://github.com/oppia/oppia-android/blob/fcb87dc79074450f90a658c9dddb186a12ab75f3/domain/src/main/java/org/oppia/android/domain/profile/ProfileManagementController.kt#L94) -> funs `initializeLearnerId()`
- [ProfileChooserViewModel](https://github.com/oppia/oppia-android/blob/fcb87dc79074450f90a658c9dddb186a12ab75f3/app/src/main/java/org/oppia/android/app/profile/ProfileChooserViewModel.kt#L22) -> fun `retrieveProfiles()`
- [RecyclerViewBindingAdapter](https://github.com/oppia/oppia-android/blob/3ffeedf7e90795ae9b23ec600a19d7cff72f1ca4/app/src/main/java/org/oppia/android/app/recyclerview/RecyclerViewBindingAdapter.java#L20)
- [BindableAdapter](https://github.com/oppia/oppia-android/blob/3ffeedf7e90795ae9b23ec600a19d7cff72f1ca4/app/src/main/java/org/oppia/android/app/recyclerview/BindableAdapter.kt#L42)

**Personal Note:**
I personally tried using `DiffUtil` for the `profile_recycler_view`, and it solved the problem. After applying it, the list updates smoothly without shifts or temporary wrong colors.

issues.title: Ensure the ELF reader works for objects built without BTF
issues.body:
Follow-up to https://github.com/cilium/ebpf/pull/1807.

Loading BPF objects without BTF info has always been supported, and although there's little reason to disable compiling with BTF nowadays, we should have at least some tests that somewhat verify this doesn't regress. Some users may not need BTF or don't want their users to be able to inspect it. Either we decide to always require BTF (feels heavy-handed and unnecessary), or we ensure it keeps working.

Some suggestions:
- Build loader.c without BTF on the latest toolchain. Most map defs are BTF, but there are still some legacy ones. Add a test that loads it and compares the CollectionSpec to a well-known definition like `TestLoadCollectionSpec`.
- Separate .c file with a subset of loader.c to lower the footprint of the test.
- Run some discovery in the code base to find code paths that require BTF and make sure proper errors are returned and there are no panics.

issues.title: Landscape layouts
issues.body:
Oppia's landscape mode support has been mostly implemented, but there are remaining TODO items in the codebase that need to be addressed to fully complete this feature. This issue tracks the final steps needed to enable landscape mode across the app.

### Background
Many users prefer landscape mode in apps, and Oppia's player view has good potential to better leverage landscape orientation (e.g., having content & interactions side-by-side rather than top-on-bottom). The core landscape functionality has been implemented, but several TODOs referencing issue #56 still need to be resolved.

### Remaining Tasks
#### ⏳ Task 1: Remove Portrait Orientation Lock from Manifest Files

**Files to modify:**
- `app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml` (Line 11)
- `instrumentation/src/java/AndroidManifest.xml` (Line 8)

**What to do:**
1. Locate the TODO comment: `<!-- TODO(#56): Reenable landscape support. -->`
2. Remove `android:screenOrientation="portrait"` from the following activities:
   - `.SplashActivity` (stretching issue has been resolved via #2652)
   - `.MyDownloadsActivity` (activity is not user-visible, so no UX impact)
3. After removing the portrait locks, delete the TODO comment since no activities are hardcoded to portrait orientation anymore

**Why this is needed:**
These manifest entries were preventing landscape mode from working. Since the underlying issues have been fixed, we can now safely remove these restrictions.


#### ⏳ Task 2: Remove @Ignore Annotations from Passing Tests

**Files to modify:**
- `app/src/sharedTest/java/org/oppia/android/app/testing/FractionInputInteractionViewTestActivityTest.kt` (Line 287)
- `app/src/sharedTest/java/org/oppia/android/app/player/audio/AudioFragmentTest.kt` (Line 363)
- `app/src/sharedTest/java/org/oppia/android/app/testing/InputInteractionViewTestActivityTest.kt` (Line 217)
- `app/src/sharedTest/java/org/oppia/android/app/testing/TextInputInteractionViewTestActivityTest.kt` (Line 173)
- `app/src/sharedTest/java/org/oppia/android/app/testing/RatioInputInteractionViewTestActivityTest.kt` (Line 178)

**What to do:**
1. Locate test methods with `@Ignore` annotations that have TODO comments referencing #56
2. Remove the `@Ignore` annotation from these test methods
3. Remove the associated TODO comment
4. Run the tests to verify they pass (they should, as the underlying issues have been resolved)

**Why this is needed:**
These tests were ignored because landscape mode wasn't working properly. Now that landscape support is functional, we can re-enable these tests to ensure continued functionality.

#### ⏳Task 3: Add tests in `StateFragmentTest` with Proper Configuration Change Tests

**File to modify:**
- `app/src/sharedTest/java/org/oppia/android/app/player/state/StateFragmentTest.kt` (Line 263)

**What to do:**
1. Locate the ignored test with TODO comment referencing #56
2. Remove the comment for adding tests.
3. **Add two new test methods** to verify that previous/next navigation buttons maintain their state during orientation changes:
   - `testStateFragment_configurationChange_previousButtonStateRetained()`
   - `testStateFragment_configurationChange_nextButtonStateRetained()`

**Test implementation guidance:**
- Set up a state where previous/next buttons have specific enabled/disabled states
- Trigger a configuration change (orientation change)
- Verify that the button states are preserved after the configuration change

**Why this is needed:**
The previous/next buttons now work correctly during orientation changes, so we should properly verify this functionality works as expected.

### How to Contribute

#### For New Contributors:
1. **Pick one task** from the checklist above
2. **Make the changes** as described in the task details
3. **Test your changes:**
   - For manifest changes: Test app rotation manually
   - For test changes: Run the specific test files to ensure they pass. [Running tests](https://github.com/oppia/oppia-android/wiki/Bazel-User-Guide#running-tests)
   - For Task 3: Run your new tests to verify they work correctly
4. **Submit a pull request** with a clear description of what you changed

Solving the above tasks will successfully close this issue.

issues.title: feat: implement `@asgardeo/tanstack-router package` for route protection
issues.body:
### Current Limitation

Currently, the Asgardeo React SDK only provides a wrapper package for **React Router** (`@asgardeo/react-router`) [1] to secure routes with authentication. Applications using other router libraries like **TanStack Router** do not have first-class support, which creates integration challenges:

**Current State:**
- No Asgardeo package exists for **TanStack Router**
- Developers need to manually wire authentication logic (`useAsgardeo`) into TanStack Router route definitions
- No `ProtectedRoute` equivalent for TanStack Router
- Repeated boilerplate code for securing routes
- Inconsistent developer experience compared to `@asgardeo/react-router`

[1] https://wso2.com/asgardeo/docs/sdks/react/guides/protecting-routes/

### Suggested Improvement

Create a new package: **`@asgardeo/tanstack-router`**  
This should provide seamless integration between Asgardeo authentication and **TanStack Router**, similar to what `@asgardeo/react-router` offers.

**Proposed Features:**
1. **ProtectedRoute Component / Wrapper**
   - Drop-in support for protecting TanStack Router routes
   - Example:

     ```tsx
     import { createRouteConfig, Router } from '@tanstack/react-router'
     import { ProtectedRoute } from '@asgardeo/tanstack-router'
     import { Dashboard } from './Dashboard'

     const dashboardRoute = createRouteConfig({
       path: '/dashboard',
       component: () => (
         <ProtectedRoute redirectTo="/signin">
           <Dashboard />
         </ProtectedRoute>
       )
     })
     ```

2. **Consistent Developer Experience**
   - Align with the existing `@asgardeo/react-router` API to minimize learning curve

### Please select the package issue is related to

@asgardeo/tanstack-router

### Version

current

### Reporter Checklist

- [x] I have searched the existing issues and this is not a duplicate.  
- [x] I have provided all the necessary information.  
- [x] I have verified the improvement is not available in the latest version of the package.

issues.title: Add an `reportCompressedSize` option to disable gzip size in console output
issues.body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Currently tsdown calculates a `gzip` size for each asset in the console output:

```
ℹ dist/index.js        0.10 kB │ gzip: 0.10 kB
```

Given that compression can become expensive on large projects, I would like an option to disable this calculation to improve build speed and have more concise output.

### Suggested solution

Implement a option like vite's [`reportCompressedSize`](https://vite.dev/config/build-options.html#build-reportcompressedsize) to skip this calculation. As far as I can tell, neither `tsdown` nor `rolldown` support such an option. With the option disabled above output becomes:

```
ℹ dist/index.js        0.10 kB
```

### Validations

- [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/sxzz/.github/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] Read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/sxzz/contribute).
- [x] Check that there isn't already an issue that request the same feature to avoid creating a duplicate.

issues.title: Secondary User Store Test Connection Fails on Retry After a Previous Failure, Even with Correct Configurations
issues.body:
### Description

When editing a secondary user store, if a Test Connection attempt fails, and the configurations are subsequently corrected, a retry still results in a failure—even though the configuration is valid. However, when the page is navigated away from and then revisited, the connection appears successful.

🔎 This issue is observed only when editing an existing secondary user store. It does not occur when adding a new secondary user store.

Upon inspection, it was identified that after the initial failure, the second Test Connection request sends an empty string for the connectionPassword, rather than reusing the previously provided encrypted password.

A screen recording demonstrating this behavior can be found below: https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bdbc736c-d853-450d-bb4a-e07e166598d1

📤 Request Comparison

Property | Initial Successful Request | Second Request After Failure -- | -- | -- connectionPassword | "ENCRYPTED PROPERTY" | "" (empty string) connectionURL | "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/patch-4044-shared-db?useSSL=false" | "jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/patch-4044-shared-db?useSSL=false" domain | "test" | "test" driverName | "com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver" | "com.mysql.cj.jdbc.Driver" username | "root" | "root" > ⚠️ **Note:** Ideally, the `connectionURL` should not contain `useSSL=false`. This is a known issue tracked under [#24533](https://github.com/wso2/product-is/issues/24533).

⚠️ Observed Behavior

After a failed attempt, the password is not retained. The system sends an empty string in the next request, resulting in a connection failure—even if the other configuration properties are correct.

This happens even when the “Update connection password” checkbox is not selected, which implies the password should remain unchanged.

✅ Expected Behavior

If the “Update connection password” checkbox is not selected, the previously entered encrypted password should be retained and sent in subsequent requests—unless explicitly changed by the user. Sending an empty password should be avoided unless the user clears the field manually.

### Steps to Reproduce 1. Edit an existing secondary user store. 2. Try a **valid configuration** and click **Test Connection** → observe that the connection **succeeds**. * Inspect the network request and verify that the `connectionPassword` field contains `"ENCRYPTED PROPERTY"`. 3. Now update the configuration to be **intentionally incorrect** (e.g., invalid hostname or port) and click **Test Connection** → observe that the connection **fails**. 4. Correct the configuration back to valid values **without modifying the password**. 5. Click **Test Connection** again → observe that the test **still fails**, even though the configuration is correct. * Inspect the network request again and note that the `connectionPassword` field now contains `""` (empty string). 6. Navigate to another tab and return → observe that the connection shows as **successful**, confirming that the corrected configuration was indeed valid. 📹 *Refer to the attached video above for a full demonstration.* ### Please select the area issue is related to User & Identity Administration ### Version wso2is-7.2.0-m6-SNAPSHOT ### Environment Details (with versions) N/A ### Developer Checklist - [ ] [Behavioural Change] Does this change introduce a behavioral change to the product? - [ ]  ↳ Approved by team lead - [ ]  ↳ Label `impact/behavioral-change` added - [ ] [Migration Impact] Does this change have a migration impact? - [ ]  ↳ Migration label added (e.g., `7.2.0-migration`) - [ ]  ↳ Migration issues created and linked - [ ] [New Configuration] Does this change introduce a new configuration? - [ ]  ↳ Label `config` added - [ ]  ↳ Configuration is properly documented

issues.title: Risk of KeyError in StudyStartForm.clean()
issues.body:
Just ran into this while debugging something else:

```python
# lines 750-755 in proposals/forms.py

            for n in range(nr_studies):
                if n >= 10:
                    break
                study_name = "study_name_" + str(n + 1)
                if not cleaned_data[study_name]:
                    self.add_error(study_name, _("Dit veld is verplicht."))
```


If `study_name` does not exist as a key in `cleaned_data` (or `initial` when called from `initial_clean`) everything falls apart. Because this code gets run on every stepper build and every listview that asks for `continue_url` this makes everything very fragile.

issues.title: Optional dependencies vs. dependency groups in kedro starter
issues.body:
Hi,

I have a question regarding the automatic setup of dependencies when initiating a new kedro project.

Why are the development dependencies of a new kedro project put in `optional-dependencies` and not in `dependency-groups`?

Upon `kedro new` choosing `2) Test: ...`, several packages are listed under `optional-dependencies` in the `pyproject.toml`. In my case, those were:
`[project.optional-dependencies]`
`dev = [ "pytest-cov~=3.0", "pytest-mock>=1.7.1, <2.0", "pytest~=7.2", "ruff~=0.1.8",]`

As I understood from [this github issue](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/9011), these dependencies in `optional-dependencies` are meant to be shipped, but listing them under `dependency-groups` would prevent them from being shipped.

Thanks for your time!

And cool project!

issues.title: Formalise DEFLATE and add implementation to examples
issues.body:
[Deflate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DEFLATE) is a lossless data compression file format that [zip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ZIP_(file_format)) and [gzip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gzip) are based on.

The [deflate algorithm](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc1951) would be a nice formalisation and verification exercise in HOL. The result of the formalisation effort could be used to construct a verified gzip-like executable using CakeML. 

The same compression and decompression algorithm might come in handy inside the CakeML compiler, once the compiler stores bulky constant data structures as read-only data. Such bulky constants could, for example, be the AST for the basis library or the bignum library.

This project is likely to fit the scope of an internship or MSc thesis.

In order to make our asynchronous replication feature GA, there are a couple of areas that need to be improved:
- Productionize provisioning
   - Move [log flags](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/39b20a92f94cd77d4ecc36a77c13b9c9641fb44d/pkg/builder/container_builder.go#L331) and [replication system vars](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/8ae3899ec3523669943d80458031fe8259285397/pkg/controller/replication/config.go#L97) to a config file created by an init container, dynamically generating the `serverId` based on the Pod index.
- Productionize failover/switchover
   - Align [CHANGE MASTER options](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/8ae3899ec3523669943d80458031fe8259285397/pkg/sql/sql.go#L733) with [MaxScale CHANGE MASTER options.](https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/blob/8ae3899ec3523669943d80458031fe8259285397/internal/controller/maxscale_controller_api.go#L105)

- Scaling out cluster with physical backups and snapshots

- Automated replica recovery
- Disable `replicasAllowEvenNumber` for replication
- Refactor APIs, see https://github.com/mariadb-operator/mariadb-operator/issues/1436#issuecomment-3327669683

- [x] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [x] I have confirmed this bug exists on the latest version of pandas.

- [x] (optional) I have confirmed this bug exists on the master branch of pandas.

---

#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example

Hey--I noticed while running [siuba's](https://github.com/machow/siuba) SQL unit tests that queries using the modulo operator are failing.

The issue is due to a recent change for issue #34211 in pandas setting the [no_parameters](https://github.com/pandas-dev/pandas/blame/5507452c4a675ad5453bc5f02cd68b65fe3977df/pandas/io/sql.py#L1161) argument before executing via a sqlalchemy engine. This was done to allow queries like `SELECT 1 % 2`, but causes SqlAlchemy expressions handling `%` to not always work with `read_sql`.

**Solution**. Rather than executing in a special way (`no_parameters`), I think you want to wrap a string query in SqlAlchemy.sql.text ([see here](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/13/core/tutorial.html#using-textual-sql)). This will allow both queries with `%` and the full range of SqlAlchemy expressions. WDYT?

```python
from sqlalchemy import sql, create_engine
import pandas as pd

engine = create_engine('postgresql://postgres:@localhost:5433/postgres', echo=False)
#engine = create_engine('postgresql://USERNAME:PASSWORD@localhost:PORT/DBNAME', echo=False)

# doesn't work, original issue in pandas: 'dict' object does not support indexing
engine.execute("SELECT 1 % 2")

# works, ideal solution
engine.execute(sql.text("SELECT 1 % 2" ))

# queries below broken by no_parameters change ----
pd.read_sql(sql.text("SELECT 1 % 2"), engine)

pd.read_sql(sql.select([sql.literal(1) % sql.literal(2)]), engine)

issues.title: Remove obsolete check_for before action
issues.body: When DSVGO came around we introduced that people had to consent to corresponding data privacy rules when they registered as users. But since there were already registered users in the database at this time, these users had to consent a posteriori. In order for that to happen, we scattered the `check_for_consent` before action throughout our controllers which would make sure that these legacy users also consented. But that was long ago, and since we have removed inactive users, we no longer need this before action, so it should be removed.

issues.body: ### Command build ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description When I define environment provider with `useValue` option SSR starts treating it as the singleton so this provider instance gets shared between all requests while during hydration this provider gets recreated so it goes to intial state. ```typescript makeEnvironmentProviders([ { provide: "MY_DATA_PROVIDER", useValue: {/*some object here*/}, } ]) ``` While with `useFactory` approach SSR treats it as unique instance for each request as expected: ```typescript makeEnvironmentProviders([ { provide: "MY_DATA_PROVIDER", useFactory: () => { return {/*some object here*/}; }, } ]) ``` I would expect to have new `useValue` instance for every SSR request the same way as it works with `useFactory` ### Minimal Reproduction [Repo to reproduce](https://github.com/dimamarksman/angular-ssr-use-value-issue/tree/main) this behaviour ### Exception or Error ```text ``` ### Your Environment ```text Angular CLI: 19.2.8 Node: 20.19.0 Package Manager: npm 10.8.2 OS: darwin arm64 Angular: 19.2.7 ... common, compiler, compiler-cli, core, forms ... platform-browser, platform-browser-dynamic, platform-server ... router Package Version --------------------------------------------------------- @angular-devkit/architect 0.1902.8 @angular-devkit/build-angular 19.2.8 @angular-devkit/core 19.2.8 @angular-devkit/schematics 19.2.8 @angular/cli 19.2.8 @angular/ssr 19.2.8 @schematics/angular 19.2.8 rxjs 7.8.2 typescript 5.7.3 zone.js 0.15.0 ``` ### Anything else relevant? ### Current Limitation

Add Right-to-Left (RTL) language support to the `@asgardeo/react` & `@asgardeo/nextjs` components to ensure proper internationalization for Arabic, Hebrew, and other RTL languages.
        
**Current State:**
- Components use LTR (Left-to-Right) layout assumptions
- No RTL-specific styling or layout adjustments
- Text direction not handled for RTL languages
- Icons and UI elements positioned for LTR only

**Missing RTL Features:**
- CSS logical properties not used (margin-left vs margin-inline-start)
- No `dir="rtl"` attribute handling
- Icons and arrows don't flip for RTL contexts
- Dropdown positioning assumes LTR layout
- Modal and popup positioning needs RTL consideration

### Suggested Improvement

## Implementation Plan

### 1. CSS Logical Properties
Replace physical properties with logical equivalents:
```css
/* Before */
margin-left: 16px;
text-align: left;

/* After */
margin-inline-start: 16px;
text-align: start;
```

### 2. RTL Detection Hook
```tsx
// Custom hook for RTL detection
const useRTL = () => {
  const isRTL = document.dir === 'rtl' || 
               document.documentElement.dir === 'rtl';
  return { isRTL };
};
```

### 3. Icon and Arrow Flipping
- Add `transform: scaleX(-1)` for directional icons in RTL
- Update arrow directions in dropdowns and navigation
- Flip chevron icons appropriately

- Dropdown positioning for RTL
- Icon alignment adjustments
- Menu item layout

**Modal Components:**
- Positioning and alignment
- Close button placement
- Content flow direction

### 5. Testing
```tsx
// RTL testing with Vitest
test('renders correctly in RTL mode', () => {
  document.dir = 'rtl';
  render(<OrganizationSwitcher />);
  // Test RTL-specific behavior
});
```

## Files to Update
- CSS/styled-components in all React components
- `OrganizationSwitcher` and related modal components
- Icon components for directional flipping

- Add RTL-specific tests

issues.title: plotly.JSONDataset not saved as utf-8
issues.body:
## Description
It can happen that the saved plotly.JSONDataset is not encoded as utf-8. Supplying the file system args as follows fixes the issue:
```yml 
myfile:
  filepath: myfilepath
  fs_args:
    open_args_save:
      encoding: utf-8
```
However, that should be the default behaviour. The question is why there is a problem when the encoding is not explicitly set here.

## Context
I had an issue with the encoding of saved plotly plots (as json) via the kedro data catalog. After saving the plots I could not read the plots anymore via the catalog. It failed with the error `'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe8 in position 6570: invalid continuation byte`.  Investigating that further, I managed to read those files with a different encoding (e.g. latin-1). I did not understand though why the files are not valid utf-8 in the first place. Adding that fs_args mentioned above solved the issues.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Save some plotly plot as plotly.JSONDataset with special characters.
2. Try to load that plot via the catalog again.
3. Eventually there should occur the error mentioned above.
4. Change the fs_args as indicated and repeat steps 1 and 2. Now it should work without issues.

## Expected Result
There should not be any encoding issues happening, because it is expected that files are saved as utf-8.

## Actual Result
The file was not saved in utf-8.

```
utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xe8 in position 6570: invalid continuation byte
```

## Your Environment
Include as many relevant details about the environment in which you experienced the bug:

* Kedro version used (`pip show kedro` or `kedro -V`): 0.19.5
* Kedro plugin and kedro plugin version used (`pip show kedro-airflow`): 3.0.0
* Python version used (`python -V`): 3.11.7
* Operating system and version: Windows 11

issues.title: Regression when public GPG key not provided and signing.verify = false
issues.body:
The below commit introduced a possible regression in 1.20.0 compared to 1.19:

https://github.com/jreleaser/jreleaser/commit/ffb02398d919d4b3818d80e5f1b7cb4cf06e1dc7#diff-9b8678cd528d74dcc05e655f431d1ac1c3ff0a061df7b811e82faa5126a28bf4L473-L487

Before this commit, it was possible to omit the GPG public key if `signing.verify` is false. After that commit, this is not possible anymore.

### Task List

- [x] Steps to reproduce provided
- [x] Stacktrace (if present) provided
- [x] Example that reproduces the problem (link to git repository is ideal)
- [x] Full description of the issue provided (see below)

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Setup Jreleaser Gradle plugin with `signing.verify = false`
2. Set up env vars `JRELEASER_GPG_PASSPHRASE` and `JRELEASER_GPG_SECRET_KEY` to valid values (note that `JRELEASER_GPG_PUBLIC_KEY` is not set)
3. Invoke `./gradlew jreleaserFullRelease` (in dry run mode is enough)

You can look at this Git repo for a full example: https://github.com/dremio/iceberg-auth-manager. Look at this file more precisely: 

https://github.com/dremio/iceberg-auth-manager/blob/86dc6828666d30c3e0375e33a38618d094aa37fb/.github/workflows/release.yml#L134-L144

Failed CI release: https://github.com/dremio/iceberg-auth-manager/actions/runs/17970383650/job/51111362440

### Expected Behaviour

Successful release.

### Actual Behaviour

The release fails with:

```
Error:  JReleaser failed after 10.097 s
org.jreleaser.model.JReleaserException: Did not find public key for signing. Ensure a value has been configured and properly formatted without indentation
```

I believe the commit mentioned above now forces a public GPG key to be provided, only to check that it's valid, cf. method `AbstractMavenDeployer.verifyKeyIsValid`. It should imho be possible to skip this check entirely if the public key is not provided, and just assume that it is valid – which was the behavior prior to this change.

issues.title: `ManagedMetric`: add new field `spec.target`
issues.body:
**What would you like to be added**:
Right now, when looking at the `Metric` and the `ManagedMetric` resource, you will see that the `spec` differs a bit from each other.

`Metric` groups GVK under `spec.target`...
```yaml
apiVersion: metrics.openmcp.cloud/v1alpha1
kind: Metric
metadata:
  name: metric-pod-count
spec:
  ...
  target:
    kind: Pod
    group: ""
    version: v1
  ...
```
On the other side, `ManagedMetric` has the GVK configuration directly under `spec`: 
```yaml
apiVersion: metrics.openmcp.cloud/v1alpha1
kind: ManagedMetric
metadata:
  name: managed-metric
spec:
  ...
  kind: Release
  group: helm.crossplane.io
  version: v1beta1
  ...
```

We should align that in the `ManagedMetric` as well and and reuse `GroupVersionKind` struct in the `spec` as well:

https://github.com/openmcp-project/metrics-operator/blob/1798cee1a90eac77a06bd918c8b6dce5b99bbf2b/api/v1alpha1/common_types.go#L15-L23

**Why is this needed**:
This is needed to have better consistency between the APIs.

issues.title: Support adding attachments to e-mails
issues.body:
## What would you like to be added:

Uno Platform implementation of `EmailManager` currently does not support e-mail attachments. The problem is that Andorid and iOS support file-based attachments only, however UWP API is fully based on streams. There would be two options:

- **Take the stream, write to file, use that file as an attachment, then clean it up "sometime" afterward** - as it means the API would eat up storage space, which could potentially be in MB range, and there would have to be a check to clean it up even in case something fails. Ideally the file should be stored in the `ApplicationData.Current.TemporaryFolder`, as that one should get cleaned up by the system automatically
- **Add some Uno-specific methods, that would allow adding file-based attachments** - this API could be either Android and iOS specific, or it could exist as a universal extension method, that would work on UWP as well, so it could be truly cross-platform.

## Why is this needed:

To send files with e-mail. It is often used for sending crash-dumps.

issues.title: Enhance Authentication with JWT
issues.body:
# Enhance Authentication with JWT

## Description
Currently, the authentication system only uses **bcrypt** for password hashing. While bcrypt secures user passwords, we still need a proper session management mechanism.  
Integrating **JWT (JSON Web Tokens)** will allow us to provide secure, stateless authentication for users.  

## Proposed Solution
- Keep **bcrypt** for password hashing (no changes needed here).  
- On successful login, generate a **JWT token** signed with a secret key.  
- Send the token back to the client (store in **HTTP-only cookie** or local storage).  
- Create an Express middleware to **verify JWT tokens** for protected routes.  
- Add token expiration handling (e.g., 1h).  
- Update logout functionality to remove/clear the token.  

## Benefits
- Adds proper session management to the existing bcrypt-based authentication.  
- Ensures secure communication between frontend (React) and backend (Node/Express).  
- Stateless and scalable, no need to maintain server-side sessions.  
- Prepares the app for future role-based authentication and third-party login integration.  

## Tech Stack
- **Backend:** Node.js, Express.js, MongoDB, JWT, bcrypt  
- **Frontend:** React (handle login/signup forms, token storage, route protection)  

## Additional Notes
- Consider implementing **refresh tokens** for long-term session management.  
- Add proper error messages for expired or invalid tokens.  
- Future improvement: OAuth (Google, GitHub login).

issues.title: Replace interpreter's use of String() for output
issues.body:
The interpreter uses the String() method for output.
This has the effect of always escaping unicode characters, which is undesirable.
See discussion https://github.com/google/mangle/discussions/60

The suggested fix is to have interpreter use an alternative conversion from ast.Constant to String that does not escape.
(Changing String() implementation is not desirable at this point, since a lot of code depends on its behavior).

issues.title: Fix n_alive component counting
issues.body:
Lucius has noticed that the n_alive_0.1 metric always looks like garbage. E.g. in this tms_40-10-id [run](https://wandb.ai/goodfire/spd/runs/dsn94977), the n_alive_0.1 value jumps around at about 40 for the hidden_layers. We're expecting it to take a value of 10, because we just need 10 dense subcomponents to represent this identity transformation.

Recall that the alive components are measured by "If the component fires over the last 4M samples (batch size 4k), then consider it alive".

It appears that on some runs there are just some components that fire occasionally with small-ish causal importance values, though sometimes up to 0.8 (if I set a threshold of 0.8 then the above experiment usually does converge to 10 alive components, as we'd expect).

Other runs don't seem to have this property, and converge much sooner (e.g. like this [run](https://wandb.ai/goodfire/spd/runs/d1jxxmhr) which uses the inserted identity layers from [PR141](https://github.com/goodfire-ai/spd/pull/141)).

Adding weight decay didn't seem to improve things on my very rough test.

Note that another reason why we might see inflated n_alive_components is if a dead component effectively "swaps" with an alive component during training. From a very preliminary test I don't think this is happening: I stopped updating gradients after a bunch of steps and noticed similar n_alive values.

Temporary Solution
Setting the ci_alive_threshold to something like 0.3 will give you close to optimal scores on tms_40-10-id. It's probably OK to use a value like this for LM experiments. But we should at some point try and get this cleaner in the toy models (and test on other toy models, which I'm yet to do.

It might also be useful to track multiple values for this metric in wandb, e.g. 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.8.

Note that we need this to be able to tell if our [inserted identity matrices](https://github.com/goodfire-ai/spd/pull/141) are being decomposed correctly

issues.title: `Package.Current.Id` Not providing right `Build/Revision` number for mobile
issues.body:
### Current behavior

The current Uno implementation only make use of `versionName` for Android and `CFBundleShortVersionString` for iOS when it should also use `versionCode` for Android and `CFBundleVersion` for iOS as `Build/Revision` value.
See [Uno documentation](https://platform.uno/docs/articles/features/windows-applicationmodel.html) for more details.

So currently we must use a version with 4 numbers if we want to have the `Build/Revision` information in our application but on iOS they must absolutely be separated because the version as to be composed of 3 numbers.
See [Apple documentation](https://developer.apple.com/library/archive/technotes/tn2420/_index.html) for more details.

The implementation should resemble Xamarin/MAUI Essentials a bit more for application version reading.
See [MAUI repositery](https://github.com/dotnet/maui/tree/main/src/Essentials/src/AppInfo) for more details.

### Expected behavior

Revision value should use `versionCode` for Android and `CFBundleVersion` for iOS or we should have an extension for the build if it's more than one digit. Whatever is best to make use of every mobile version variable.

### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)

No sample needed, it's working but limiting our application.

### Workaround

Use Xamarin/MAUI Essentials.

### Works on UWP/WinUI

Yes

### Environment

Uno.UI / Uno.UI.WebAssembly / Uno.UI.Skia, Uno.WinUI / Uno.WinUI.WebAssembly / Uno.WinUI.Skia
